evidence: First half holds: rls.py:335 calls tree.sql(dialect=dialect, normalize_functions=False); sqlglot generator.py:1126-1131 normalize_func returns the name unchanged, and anonymous_sql (generator.py:4204-4211) prints the Anonymous name as written (qualified ones are never normalised anyway). Known functions like Count print via their uppercase sql_name, so count(*) -> COUNT(*). Second half is wrong as a general statement: the doc (docs/external/row-level-security.md:121) says strpos(a, 'x') is printed as POSITION('x' IN a) with no dialect qualifier, but the printer is dialect-specific. Only PostgreSQL maps exp.StrPosition to POSITION (sqlglot/generators/postgres.py:416, strposition_sql func_name=POSITION, dialects/dialect.py:1546-1547). SQLite prints INSTR(a, 'x') (generators/sqlite.py:168) and MySQL uses the LOCATE form (generators/mysql.py:199, dialect.py:1549 swaps args for LOCATE). SQL Lens supports postgres/mysql/sqlite, so for two of three dialects the documented example output is wrong. I could not run code (no shell), so the MySQL/SQLite output is traced from source, not executed. The doc does say output 'can differ in spelling', but the concrete example is stated as fact without naming PostgreSQL.

Traced by reading sqlglot 30.27.0 (the installed .venv version, per dist-info) rather than executing it. rls.py:335 calls tree.sql(dialect=dialect, normalize_functions=False). In sqlglot generator.py:4204-4211 anonymous_sql prints the name through self.func, and normalize_func (generator.py:1126-1131) returns the name unchanged when normalize_functions is False. So an unrecognised function keeps its written case and quotes. Absolute-claim input traced: postgres "quote_ident"(name) parses to Anonymous with a quoted identifier and is printed as written. For strpos, generators/postgres.py:416 maps exp.StrPosition to strposition_sql(func_name="POSITION"). dialect.py:1546-1547 then builds Anonymous POSITION(In(substr, string)), which prints POSITION('x' IN a). For count(*), Count prints through function_fallback_sql -> function_name -> sql_name() 'COUNT' (generator.py:4915-4931). Postgres sets no ORIGINAL_NAME_META_KEY (only drill, bigquery and clickhouse do), so the written case is not retained and COUNT(*) is printed. The doc claim at row-level-security.md:107 matches. The cited test only asserts {'position','strpos'} & params, which is loose but not wrong.

rls.py:332-335 serialises with tree.sql(dialect=dialect, normalize_functions=False), per its comment because the default upper-cases unrecognised (Anonymous) function names. A case-insensitive grep of every .py file in an installed sqlglot package (a venv found under /tmp, not the head view) finds 'printf' only in duckdb generator SQL strings, so no parser FUNCTIONS map, including sqlite's, maps PRINTF to a typed expression. It is therefore parsed as exp.Anonymous, which is upper-cased by default (PRINTF) and keeps its written case with normalize_functions=False. SQLite documents that an unaliased result column is named after the expression text as written, so the column name follows the emitted case. The test case at tests/unit/test_safety_rls.py:240-244 matches the changelog example (changelog.d/355.fixed.md:4-7). The sqlglot version checked may differ from the project's pinned one; the test only checks the SQL string, not the column name.
